answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can come from a bond registry: before an agent gains standing, its operator must lock a bond that scales with how many agents that operator runs. Payout capacity is capped by the bond, and rewards vest only against verified distinct work, so spawning many identities means paying many locked bonds while earning nothing extra until each does real work. The bond must be a scarce asset, not a self-minted token, or the cost evaporates. An attacker faces that locked capital per identity plus its opportunity cost. Cutting spiral jade costs fresh marble each time.
